note: Every question is split into what is held, what is missing, what it blocks and what closes it. 'answered' is used only where a number on file settles the question, and that number is quoted in the held cell.

questions.question: May any market number be published at all?
questions.held: NFL.com section 1.3 permits individual non-commercial informational use and prohibits systematic retrieval without written consent. No odds publisher is registered.
questions.missing: A written permission, or a price source whose terms permit republication of the number.
questions.blocks: Every market column, every residual against the market, every ROI and CLV claim, every reward.
questions.closes: A licence or a permitted source is recorded in research/sources.json with its terms quoted.

questions.question: Is there a source that prints an opening and a closing number for NFL games?
questions.held: The repository's own price desks record closing observations from a secondary publisher; this desk registers none.
questions.missing: One publisher that prints both an opening and a closing number with timestamps and that permits the use.
questions.blocks: R01 and R18: an opening/closing store and a residual against the market.
questions.closes: A registered source whose page prints both numbers for the same game.

questions.question: Who actually started, as opposed to who was expected to start?
questions.held: 3 dated announced-starter statements (Seattle, Cleveland, Arizona) and 6 club depth charts, both read 2026-11-17.
questions.missing: An official participation record: an inactive list, a Game Book or a snap count. 0 of 136 games are covered.
questions.blocks: R10 (the availability graph), R25, R123, R124 and the cross-side mismatch matrix.
questions.closes: One Game Book or inactive list per captured game, joined to the expected starter.

questions.question: Is the printed depth chart the right source for depth order?
questions.held: 26 of 32 clubs serve a text chart; this desk verified 6 of them by reading them. Houston serves an image.
questions.missing: A club-by-club verification of the remaining 26, and a structured source for Houston.
questions.blocks: Route (a) for all 32 clubs, which is what R77/R78 require before any backup-deficiency feature.
questions.closes: 32 of 32 clubs read and parsed from text.

questions.question: What does each game designation actually mean on the field?
questions.held: 216 game designations across 347 report rows, from one dated read (70 Out, 11 Doubtful, 90 Questionable, 176 blank).
questions.missing: The play outcome behind each designation. Without it a designation is a label, not a probability.
questions.blocks: R61, R79, R80 and any model that uses an injury label as a feature.
questions.closes: Designations joined to inactive lists across at least 200 player-games per designation.

questions.question: Is 'not on the report' the same as 'available'?
questions.held: The Week 10 report lists 347 rows for 28 clubs. No reserve or injured-reserve list is captured, so an absent name cannot be explained.
questions.missing: The 32 roster pages' reserve sections, or a transaction log that states IR placements.
questions.blocks: R13, R99, R100: any claim that a club is healthy because a name is missing.
questions.closes: 32 of 32 reserve lists captured with dates.

questions.question: How many players does one report actually cover, and are the inherited counts right?
questions.held: 347 rows, 28 clubs (the 4 bye clubs have no section), 171 rows with a game designation. Recomputed from the live page on 2026-11-17.
questions.missing: Nothing for the count itself. The count is settled.
questions.blocks: Nothing; the stale 254/6 figures are corrected here.
questions.closes: Settled: 347 rows and 171 designations is the live count.

questions.question: Can a venue be published for every fixture from an official page?
questions.held: 12 of 13 Week 11 fixtures print a stadium string in the schedule page's own ticket and hotel links; the Mexico City game prints a label, not a stadium.
questions.missing: A league or club page that prints the stadium for the international fixture.
questions.blocks: R23: complete venue transcription.
questions.closes: 13 of 13 fixtures with a printed stadium.

questions.question: Is there an official dated schedule announcement to publish beside the live schedule?
questions.held: Two dated documents are cited: the flexible-scheduling procedures page and the dated Week 16-18 TBD announcement text.
questions.missing: Nothing for the requirement. It is met.
questions.blocks: Nothing.
questions.closes: Settled.

questions.question: Does weather belong in the model?
questions.held: Nothing: no forecast feed and no roof/surface register are captured. One page prints a 'Clear' label.
questions.missing: A registered hourly forecast source and a stadium roof/surface register.
questions.blocks: R89 and R90, and any totals or passing-prop adjustment for wind.
questions.closes: A forecast grid per stadium plus a roof register.

questions.question: Is the side signal real?
questions.held: The best side entry scores +0.057 Brier skill on weeks 6-9 (n=57), cluster lower bound +0.015, family-wise p 0.348 over 21 trials.
questions.missing: A prospective window of pre-kickoff forecasts, and enough games for the required-n bar.
questions.blocks: Any claim of skill. The family null does not clear.
questions.closes: A prospective window with a cluster lower bound above zero after adjustment.

questions.question: Is the total signal real?
questions.held: No. Every total entry sits within 0.024 Brier skill of zero, and the best total entry has a negative lower bound.
questions.missing: Nothing to answer this question; it is answered negatively.
questions.blocks: Any total-based strategy.
questions.closes: Settled: the total model is not distinguishable from the benchmark on this window.

questions.question: Does the ranking survive the development window?
questions.held: No: the development order and the evaluation order agree in 1 of 21 positions.
questions.missing: A longer corpus, or a prospective window.
questions.blocks: Trusting the ranking as a property of the model rather than of weeks 6-9.
questions.closes: A window in which the order is stable across halves.

questions.question: How many selections before an edge would even be visible?
questions.held: 2,241 settled selections for a 55% model at 80% power, or 173 weeks at this season's 13 games a week.
questions.missing: Nothing; the arithmetic is settled.
questions.blocks: Any short-window reward or ranking claim.
questions.closes: Settled.

questions.question: Can two legs in the same game be multiplied?
questions.held: No. Measured phi for side x total is -0.096 (n=120, 95% interval -0.271 to +0.085); side x moneyline is +0.935 (n=120).
questions.missing: A directly validated joint probability at the exact thresholds, plus the operator's void/push rule.
questions.blocks: Every same-game parlay and prop combo.
questions.closes: An operator rule registered and a joint probability validated on a prospective sample.

questions.question: Is a player prop combination measurable at all here?
questions.held: No player-level outcome is captured. 0 prop lines, 0 prop outcomes.
questions.missing: Per-player per-game logs for the players in each proposed pair.
questions.blocks: R119 and the prop-combo division.
questions.closes: A per-player game log for every player in a proposed combination.

questions.question: May the collection be automated?
questions.held: No. Section 1.3 prohibits systematic retrieval without written consent, so no schedule is enabled and each capture is a single targeted read.
questions.missing: Written consent, or an authorised structured feed.
questions.blocks: R31, R33, R34, R51, R52, R67 and every daily-series requirement.
questions.closes: A consent record or an authorised feed.

questions.question: Is one capture a series?
questions.held: No. Three dated captures exist for this desk; a delta needs two reads of the same scope and a trend needs more.
questions.missing: Daily captures from Wednesday to kickoff.
questions.closes: Two reads of the same scope with timestamps.

questions.question: Does availability information improve the model?
questions.held: Unknown by construction. The 'with personnel' arm is empty because no absence is confirmed in the corpus.
questions.missing: Confirmed absences per game, from inactive lists or Game Books.
questions.blocks: R27, R28, R29, R30 and the personnnel weighting of the originated line.
questions.closes: 136 games with a confirmed absence set.

questions.question: Is a fixed points penalty for a missing starter defensible?
questions.held: No test in this repository supports one. The pipeline contains 0 fixed penalties.
questions.missing: The same evidence the ablation needs; a penalty is a placeholder for it.
questions.blocks: Any injury-adjusted line.
questions.closes: A measured effect with an interval, not a constant.

questions.question: Can a reward be paid?
questions.held: No. 0 of 21 entries qualify: V7 (price) and V8 (prospective record) cannot pass.
questions.missing: A price, a prospective record, and a funding decision.
questions.blocks: R118 and the whole reward schedule.
questions.closes: One entry passing V1-V8.

questions.question: Should the leaderboard rank on return?
questions.held: No. Return at n=57 is dominated by the noise term; the power table shows why.
questions.missing: Nothing; the proposal is rejected with arithmetic.
questions.blocks: Nothing.
questions.closes: Settled: rejected.

questions.question: Is the leaderboard free of backtest numbers presented as results?
questions.held: Yes. Every entry is labelled `evaluation weeks 6-9` and every one is `qualified: false`.
questions.missing: Nothing.
questions.blocks: Nothing.
questions.closes: Settled, and enforced by a build check.

questions.question: Is the pre-registration prospective?
questions.held: No. It was written after weeks 1-9 were played, and it says so on every page that cites it.
questions.missing: A window that opens after the registration is committed.
questions.blocks: Any prospective claim, and V8.
questions.closes: A forecast recorded before its kickoff.

questions.question: Can the previous desks' claims be inherited without re-checking?
questions.held: The specific claims that were re-read did not reproduce (Baltimore's quarterback row, Washington's empty slot). Each is flagged with the fresh text.
questions.missing: A re-read of every claim in every desk, which no desk has done line by line.
questions.blocks: Any cross-desk synthesis presented as verified fact.
questions.closes: A re-read of the claim against the publisher, recorded with the text.

questions.question: What is the single most useful next purchase of information?
questions.held: The cheapest large gain would be inactive lists: they turn 'suspected replacement' into 'confirmed replacement' and unblock the ablation.
questions.missing: The lists themselves.
questions.blocks: Q03, Q19 and R25 all close on the same datum.
questions.closes: One season of inactive lists.
